1	**PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL** **ATTORNEY-CLIENT PRIVILEGED** **ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT**
2	
3	**INTERNAL MEMORANDUM**
4	
5	**TO:** Eleanor Voss, Partner Thornwell & Pratt LLP 1200 K Street NW, Suite 800 Washington, DC 20005
6	
7	**CC:** Jason Kiel, Senior Associate Thornwell & Pratt LLP
8	
9	**FROM:** David Yun-Nakamura, General Counsel Greenfield Organics, Inc.
10	
11	**DATE:** October 15, 2024
12	
13	**RE:** Civil Investigative Demand No. 28-47293 --- Background Information and Initial Observations
14	
15	Eleanor,
16	
17	I am writing to provide you and the Thornwell & Pratt team with background information regarding Civil Investigative Demand No. 28-47293 recently served on Greenfield Organics, Inc. This memorandum summarizes the relevant facts, identifies several issues I would like your guidance on, and attaches key documents for your review. The contents of this memorandum are intended to be protected by the attorney-client privilege and the work product doctrine. Please treat this memorandum and its attachments accordingly.
18	
19	**[1. Introduction and Purpose]{.underline}**
20	
21	On October 2, 2024, the Antitrust Division of the United States Department of Justice issued Civil Investigative Demand No. 28-47293 in connection with a federal investigation captioned *In the Matter of Organic Baby Food Products*. The CID was served on Greenfield\'s registered agent, DC Statutory Agent, located at 150 Fayetteville Street, Suite 300, Raleigh, NC 27601, on October 4, 2024. DC Statutory Agent forwarded the CID to my attention, and I received it the same day.
22	
23	The CID references potential violations of Sections 1 and 2 of the Sherman Act, 15 U.S.C. §§ 1 and 2, and was issued pursuant to the Antitrust Civil Process Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1312. The cover letter identifies Senior Trial Attorney Patricia Rourke of the Healthcare and Consumer Products Section as the lead DOJ attorney on the investigation. The CID is addressed to Greenfield Organics, Inc. and demands the production of documentary materials, responses to written interrogatories, and oral testimony, as I describe in greater detail in Section 3 below.
24	
25	As you know, Thornwell & Pratt has represented Greenfield on regulatory and compliance matters since 2018, and I am confident your team has the institutional knowledge and expertise needed to guide us through this process. The purpose of this memorandum is to provide you with comprehensive background information on Greenfield\'s business operations, the relevant factual landscape, and my initial observations on certain topics that may warrant further discussion. I have tried to be thorough but concise, and I expect we will cover a number of these topics in more detail once you have had an opportunity to review the attached materials.
26	
27	With respect to key deadlines, the CID specifies a return date for documentary materials and interrogatory responses of November 18, 2024. Oral testimony from \"persons most knowledgeable\" is scheduled for November 22, 2024, at the DOJ\'s offices in Washington. I understand there may also be a deadline to petition for modification or to set aside the CID under the statute, which I believe falls around October 24. I would appreciate your guidance on the procedural calendar and any actions we should be considering in the near term. I expect many of these topics will be best addressed on a call, and I am happy to set one up at your earliest convenience.
28	
29	**[2. Company Overview]{.underline}**
30	
31	Greenfield Organics, Inc. is a Delaware corporation headquartered at 2100 Capital Boulevard, Raleigh, NC 27604. The company was founded in 2009, and over the past fifteen years it has grown into a vertically integrated organic food manufacturer and distributor with a national retail footprint. Our primary product lines are organic baby food, toddler snacks, and infant formula, all of which are sold under the \"PureSprout\" brand. The PureSprout brand is well recognized among consumers in the organic and natural food segment and is carried by major national retailers including Whole Foods, Target, Kroger, and Publix, as well as through direct-to-consumer e-commerce channels.
32	
33	In terms of product scope, we currently maintain 159 active SKUs across the three product categories: 47 baby food SKUs, 89 toddler snack SKUs, and 23 infant formula SKUs. The baby food line includes single-ingredient purees, multi-ingredient blends, and pouched meals for infants aged four months through twelve months. The toddler snack line includes puffs, bars, and fruit-and-vegetable bites for children aged twelve months through thirty-six months. The infant formula line was launched in 2019 and includes three formulations in various package sizes.
34	
35	For the fiscal year ending December 31, 2023, Greenfield reported total annual revenue of approximately \$487 million and EBITDA of \$62.3 million. The PureSprout organic baby food segment alone accounted for approximately \$341 million in revenue, representing roughly 70% of total company revenue. Gross margins on the organic baby food segment were 38.2% for fiscal year 2023. Based on our internal market analysis and third-party data, we estimate that Greenfield holds approximately 28% of the U.S. organic baby food market.
36	
37	Greenfield currently employs approximately 1,840 people across three manufacturing and distribution facilities: our headquarters campus in Raleigh, North Carolina; a production facility at 450 Industrial Parkway, Bend, OR 97701; and a production and distribution center at 1875 Overland Road, Boise, ID 83705. We also maintain a small sales office in Bentonville, Arkansas to support the Walmart and Sam\'s Club accounts, though that office does not handle production or distribution.
38	
39	The CID appears to be focused primarily on the organic baby food segment, which makes sense given the investigation caption. However, I wanted to flag that our internal product classification and pricing structures do not always draw clean lines between the baby food, toddler snack, and infant formula categories. I\'m not sure whether the CID\'s references to \"organic baby food products\" are intended to cover our toddler snack and formula lines as well --- they\'re marketed under the same PureSprout brand and sometimes share pricing structures. For example, several of our toddler snack products are packaged and priced using the same per-ounce wholesale framework as our baby food products, and some retailers shelve them together. This may be relevant as we evaluate the scope of the document demands.
40	
41	**[3. Summary of the CID\'s Key Demands]{.underline}**
42	
43	The CID contains three categories of demands, which I summarize below. The full CID is attached for your review.
44	
45	**Documentary Material Demands.** The CID includes fourteen specifications requesting documentary materials spanning the period from January 1, 2019 to the present. The specifications cover a wide range of topics, and I expect the document collection and review effort to be substantial. Let me highlight the specifications I consider most significant:
46	
47	DMD Specification 3 requests \"all documents and communications relating to pricing of organic baby food products,\" broadly defined, from January 1, 2019 to the present. Given the volume of pricing-related communications across our sales, marketing, and finance teams over that period, this specification alone could generate an enormous number of responsive documents. Our IT department has estimated that keyword searches across our email and document management systems could return hundreds of thousands of hits for Specification 3 alone. This is going to be the single largest driver of cost and burden in the production.
48	
49	DMD Specification 7 requests all documents exchanged between Greenfield and any competitor, including NourishCo, relating to pricing, output, capacity, market allocation, or customer allocation. I discuss the Hollister-Felding communications in Section 4 below, which will be the most significant responsive category here.
50	
51	DMD Specification 9 requests all documents relating to the Organic Infant Nutrition Trade Association, or OINTA, including meeting agendas, minutes, presentations, and communications between members. I discuss OINTA in Section 6 below.
52	
53	DMD Specification 11 requests all documents prepared by or for any consultant or advisor relating to competitive analysis, market share, or competitive strategy. This would pick up the Ridgeline report, which I discuss further in Section 5 below.
54	
55	DMD Specification 14 requests all documents relating to any agreement, understanding, or arrangement between Greenfield and any other manufacturer or distributor regarding terms of sale to retailers. This is quite broad and could encompass routine co-marketing and cooperative merchandising agreements.
56	
57	**Interrogatories.** The CID contains eight interrogatories. Of particular note, Interrogatory 4 requires us to identify all communications between Greenfield officers, directors, or employees and NourishCo officers, directors, or employees from January 1, 2020 to the present. Interrogatory 6 requires us to describe all pricing methodologies used for the PureSprout brand from January 1, 2021 to the present, including the identity of persons involved in pricing decisions and any external sources of data or analysis relied upon. The remaining interrogatories cover corporate structure, distribution agreements, manufacturing capacity, and market share calculations.
58	
59	**Oral Testimony.** The CID demands oral testimony from \"persons most knowledgeable\" regarding pricing decisions, distribution arrangements, and trade association activities. Testimony is scheduled for November 22, 2024, at DOJ offices in Washington, D.C.
60	
61	**Estimated Volume and Cost.** Our IT department has conducted a preliminary assessment and estimates that there are approximately 1.2 million potentially responsive documents across our various data systems, before any custodian filtering or de-duplication. At estimated review rates and with the use of technology-assisted review tools, outside vendor costs for processing, hosting, and review could run upwards of \$2 million. I recognize we may be able to reduce this through custodian prioritization and negotiation with DOJ over the scope, and I welcome your thoughts on approach.
62	
63	I should also note for completeness that the CID was signed by Senior Trial Attorney Patricia Rourke, acting by authority of the Assistant Attorney General. I have attached the full CID with the cover letter and signature page for your review.
64	
65	**[4. The Hollister-Felding Communications]{.underline}**
66	
67	I want to provide some context regarding the communications between our CEO, Margaret \"Meg\" Hollister, and the CEO of NourishCo, Robert Felding. Meg and Robert have a personal relationship that predates both of their tenures at their respective companies. They were classmates at the University of Virginia Darden School of Business, graduating together in the class of 2005. They have maintained a friendship over the years, and they communicate with some regularity via text message and personal email.
68	
69	At my request, our IT department worked with Meg to compile a log of her communications with Felding. This effort involved a review of Meg\'s personal text messages and personal email account, which Meg made available voluntarily. Based on this review, we identified approximately 47 text messages and 12 emails between Hollister and Felding from January 2020 through September 2024, totaling 59 individual communications. I have attached the log compiled by IT for your reference as hollister-felding-comms-log.xlsx.
70	
71	The substantial majority of these communications are personal in nature. They consist of catching up on personal matters, discussions about Darden alumni events and reunion planning, family updates, sports, travel, and similar topics entirely unrelated to business. In my review, they read as the kind of messages you would expect between two old friends who happen to work in the same industry.
72	
73	That said, I want to flag that a handful of messages touch on business topics. I have identified at least six text messages and two emails that reference \"market conditions,\" \"input costs,\" or general industry trends in passing, typically in the course of broader personal conversations. In most cases, these references are fleeting --- a sentence or two in the middle of a longer exchange about other topics.
74	
75	There is one message that I think is potentially concerning and that I wanted to bring specifically to your attention. On June 14, 2022, Meg sent a text message to Felding that reads: \"We\'re looking at needing to move prices up in July. Organic oat costs are killing us. You seeing the same thing?\" Meg tells me this was just venting about commodity costs and she wasn\'t coordinating anything with Robert. I think the context of their friendship makes that plausible, but I wanted to flag it for your review.
76	
77	For context, I should note that Greenfield did implement a price increase on our organic baby food products effective July 1, 2022, raising the weighted average wholesale price from \$1.42 per ounce to \$1.58 per ounce. NourishCo also raised its prices around the same time, though I do not know the exact effective date of their increase. We had been planning that increase internally since at least May 2022 based on our own cost analysis, and the decision was driven by significant increases in organic oat, fruit, and vegetable input costs during the first half of 2022.
78	
79	More broadly, I am aware that there were four instances between mid-2022 and late 2023 in which both Greenfield and NourishCo implemented price increases within a relatively short window of each other: July 1, 2022; October 15, 2022; March 1, 2023; and September 1, 2023. Our per-ounce weighted average wholesale price progressed as follows over that period: \$1.42, to \$1.58, to \$1.71, to \$1.85, to \$1.99 per ounce --- a cumulative increase of \$0.57 per ounce, or approximately 40%. In all four instances, both companies moved prices within a short window. I understand this may look concerning from the outside, but our pricing decisions were independently driven by our own cost models. The organic baby food industry faced sustained input cost inflation throughout this period, and it would not be unusual for companies with similar cost structures to reach similar pricing conclusions.
80	
81	I should also note that the Hollister-Felding communications were conducted entirely on personal devices and personal email accounts, not through Greenfield\'s corporate systems. This means they were not captured in our standard email archive. Do we need to collect Meg\'s personal phone and email? I\'d prefer to handle that sensitively given Meg\'s role as CEO and the personal nature of much of the content.
82	
83	**[5. The Ridgeline Consulting Engagement and Report]{.underline}**
84	
85	In March 2023, Greenfield retained Ridgeline Consulting Group to conduct a competitive landscape analysis of the U.S. organic baby food market. The lead consultant on the engagement was Thomas Brennan, a managing director at Ridgeline. The fee was a fixed \$185,000 plus expenses. The engagement letter was dated March 10, 2023, and I signed it on behalf of Greenfield in my capacity as General Counsel, as our legal department manages all vendor contracts over \$100,000 as a matter of internal policy.
86	
87	The business rationale for the engagement was straightforward. We were looking to better understand our competitive position in the organic baby food segment and to inform our go-to-market strategy and pricing approach for fiscal year 2024. Ridgeline was selected based on their expertise in the natural and organic food sector. They conducted the analysis over approximately three months, and the final report --- a 78-page document --- was delivered on June 15, 2023.
88	
89	The report was distributed internally to the following individuals: Meg Hollister (CEO), Alan Prescott (CFO), Denise Waverly (VP of Sales), Craig Oshiro (VP of Marketing), and me. It was discussed at a senior leadership meeting on June 22, 2023, and portions of the analysis were subsequently referenced in our 2024 annual business plan.
90	
91	The report contains detailed market share estimates for all major competitors in the U.S. organic baby food market, including NourishCo and TinyHarvest. It also includes competitor pricing data across multiple product categories, channel-by-channel retail distribution analysis, consumer trend data, and strategic recommendations for Greenfield\'s positioning.
92	
93	I want to specifically flag one section of the report. The \"Optimal Pricing Corridors\" analysis on pages 34 through 41 recommends that Greenfield \"maintain price parity with TinyHarvest products within a ±3% band to avoid triggering retailer switching behavior.\" I think this was standard competitive benchmarking advice --- the idea being that if our prices deviate too far from comparable products on the shelf, retailers may reduce shelf space or shift promotional support. It struck me as the kind of analysis any consultant would provide.
94	
95	I should mention, however, that the engagement letter doesn\'t specifically reference that Ridgeline was working at the direction of counsel or for legal purposes. The letter describes the scope as a \"competitive landscape analysis and strategic market assessment\" and does not invoke privilege or note any connection to anticipated litigation or legal advice. I signed the letter because our legal department manages vendor contracts, not because the engagement was structured as a privileged legal consultation. I\'m wondering whether we can claim privilege over the report --- it would be responsive to DMD Specification 11, and I\'d rather not produce it if we can avoid it. The report is detailed and candid in ways that I think could be taken out of context.
96	
97	I have attached the engagement letter (ridgeline-engagement-letter.docx) and the executive summary excerpt from the report (ridgeline-report-excerpt.docx) for your review.
98

100	
101	Greenfield is a member of the Organic Infant Nutrition Trade Association, or OINTA, a Washington, D.C.-based trade association that represents manufacturers and distributors in the organic infant and toddler nutrition sector. The executive director of OINTA is Pamela Sievert. NourishCo is also a member of OINTA, as are several other companies in the organic baby food space, including TinyHarvest, BabyBright Organics, and LittleLeaf Foods.

OINTA aggregates the data across all reporting members and publishes averaged index figures with a one-quarter lag. For example, data submitted for Q1 would be published as part of the Q2 index report. The database is available to all OINTA members through a password-protected portal on the OINTA website.
106	
107	Our participation in OINTA has been routine industry engagement. The Pricing Index Database is a standard benchmarking tool --- all members contribute and the data is aggregated and published with a lag. I don\'t think our participation raises any issues, but I wanted you to be aware since DMD Specification 9 asks for all OINTA-related documents. We have a substantial volume of OINTA materials, including meeting agendas, presentation decks, email correspondence with OINTA staff, and our quarterly submissions to the Pricing Index Database.

109	**[7. Data Systems and Email Migration Issue]{.underline}**
110	
111	I want to provide an overview of Greenfield\'s data systems and flag a couple of issues that may be relevant to the document collection effort.
112	
113	Greenfield\'s current primary data systems include the following: Microsoft 365 for email, Microsoft Teams for internal messaging and collaboration, SharePoint for document management, Salesforce CRM for sales and customer relationship data, and SAP ERP for financial and operations data. We also maintain a legacy Google Workspace archive from our prior email environment.
114	
115	With respect to internal messaging, Greenfield used Slack as its primary internal communication platform from approximately 2018 through January 2024, at which point the company migrated to Microsoft Teams as part of the broader Microsoft 365 adoption. The Slack workspace was deactivated in January 2024 and data was exported to an archive.
116	
117	I need to flag two data integrity issues for your attention.

Cloudbridge delivered a summary report dated September 5, 2023, confirming that the migration was substantially complete. However, the report identified that approximately 4% of emails from the 2019--2023 period were not successfully migrated due to what Cloudbridge described as \"message formatting incompatibilities and embedded object corruption.\" Based on the total volume of emails in the Google Workspace environment, this represents approximately 14,800 unmigrated messages across all employees. I should note that we decommissioned the Google Workspace environment on October 1, 2023, per the recommendation of our IT team after Cloudbridge confirmed the migration was substantially complete. I\'m not sure whether the unmigrated emails can be recovered at this point --- we\'d need to check with Cloudbridge to determine whether any backup or archive of the Google Workspace data still exists.

121	**Server Failure.** We also had a server issue at our Raleigh facility on March 15, 2024, that resulted in the loss of approximately two weeks of local backup data covering March 1 through March 15, 2024. Our IT team investigated the failure and was unable to recover this data. The affected server hosted local backup copies of email, SharePoint documents, and certain Salesforce data exports for the Raleigh facility. Our primary cloud-hosted data was not affected, but the local backup layer for that two-week window is gone.
122	
123	I have attached the Cloudbridge migration summary report (cloudbridge-migration-report.docx) for your reference. I can also put you in touch with our IT Director, Raj Patel, if you need additional technical details.

126

128

Under this schedule, emails older than approximately October 2019 would have been automatically deleted in the ordinary course of business. Slack messages were subject to an automatic deletion policy with a 90-day retention window. Under this policy, Slack messages were automatically purged 90 days after they were sent. Since Greenfield used Slack as its primary internal communication platform from approximately 2018 through January 2024, this means that the vast majority of historical Slack messages from the 2019--2024 period would have been automatically deleted well before we received the CID. Since we stopped using Slack in January 2024 and migrated to Teams, I believe most of the relevant Slack content would have been deleted by the time we received the CID under our standard retention schedule. The Slack data export we performed at the time of the Teams migration in January 2024 captured only messages that had not yet been purged under the 90-day policy, which would have been limited to messages from approximately late October 2023 through January 2024.
130	
131	I should mention that we have not yet issued a formal litigation hold in response to the CID. We received it on October 4, and I\'ve been focused on getting this memo together for you and assembling the relevant background materials. I wanted your guidance on the scope and recipients of any hold before we circulate it. In the meantime, I\'ve informally asked our IT director, Raj Patel, to suspend any scheduled automatic deletions, but I\'m not sure that instruction has been fully implemented across all systems. Raj indicated he needed to coordinate with our Microsoft 365 administrator and the Salesforce team to modify the retention settings, and I have not yet confirmed whether that process has been completed.
132	
133	I should also note that the document retention policy does not contain a specific section addressing litigation holds or preservation obligations in the event of a government investigation or legal proceeding. This is something we probably ought to address going forward as a matter of best practice.
134	
135	**[9. Prior Common Interest Agreement with NourishCo\'s Counsel]{.underline}**
136	
137	I want to make you aware of a prior common interest agreement that may be relevant. In connection with the class action captioned *In re Organic Baby Food Labeling Litigation*, Case No. 3:21-cv-04187 (W.D. Tex.), in which both Greenfield and NourishCo were named as co-defendants, Thornwell & Pratt LLP and Fielding & Acosta LLP --- NourishCo\'s outside counsel, based in Austin, Texas --- entered into a common interest agreement dated September 15, 2021. I have attached a copy of the agreement for your reference (common-interest-agreement.docx).
138	
139	The agreement covers \"all communications between counsel for the Common Interest Parties relating to the defense of the Labeling Litigation.\" The labeling class action was ultimately settled by both Greenfield and NourishCo on April 30, 2023, and the settlement was approved by the court that summer.
140	
141	The agreement doesn\'t have a termination clause, so I\'m not entirely sure of its current status. We haven\'t had occasion to communicate with Fielding & Acosta under it since the settlement. I would appreciate your assessment of whether the agreement remains in effect and what its scope covers at this point.
142	
143	I should mention that during the labeling litigation, some of the shared communications between our counsel and Fielding & Acosta touched on market positioning, pricing strategies, and competitive dynamics --- this came up naturally in the context of defending the labeling claims, where we needed to explain our pricing and market practices to respond to the plaintiffs\' allegations about misleading pricing of organic versus conventional products. I\'m hoping those communications remain protected under the agreement, but I wanted you to be aware of the content in light of the current DOJ investigation.

**CLOUDBRIDGE SOLUTIONS** 3400 Glenwood Avenue, Suite 210 Raleigh, NC 27612 Tel: (919) 555-0184 \| www.cloudbridgesolutions.com

**Email Platform Migration --- Project Completion Summary Report**

**Report Date:** September 5, 2023

**Prepared for:** Greenfield Organics, Inc., Attn: IT Department **Project Reference:** Project No. CB-2023-0417

CONFIDENTIAL: This report is confidential and intended solely for the use of Greenfield Organics, Inc. Unauthorized distribution, copying, or disclosure of this document or its contents is prohibited without the prior written consent of Cloudbridge Solutions.

**[1. Executive Summary]{.underline}**

Cloudbridge Solutions (\"Cloudbridge\") was engaged by Greenfield Organics, Inc. (\"Greenfield\" or \"Client\") to perform a full migration of email, calendar, contacts, and file-storage data from the Client\'s existing Google Workspace environment to Microsoft 365. The migration was executed during the month of August 2023 and is now complete as of the date of this report.

The project encompassed approximately 1,840 active user mailboxes, together with approximately 100 departmental, shared, and functional mailboxes, for a total of approximately 1,940 mailboxes migrated. All mailboxes across all three of the Client\'s office locations were included within the scope of the engagement.

The overall migration success rate was 96% of all email messages successfully migrated to the target Microsoft 365 environment. Approximately 4% of email messages --- representing approximately 14,800 individual messages across all mailboxes --- were not successfully migrated. These migration failures were attributable to message formatting incompatibilities and embedded object corruption encountered during the extraction and import process. Further detail regarding the nature and distribution of these failures is provided in Section 3 of this report.

Cloudbridge considers the migration project substantially complete and is delivering this summary report in accordance with the terms of the engagement.

**[2. Project Scope and Timeline]{.underline}**

**Client:** Greenfield Organics, Inc., a Delaware corporation headquartered at 2100 Capital Boulevard, Raleigh, NC 27604.

**Engagement Start Date:** June 12, 2023, at which time the planning and environment-assessment phase commenced. The active migration execution window was August 7 through August 25, 2023.

**Source Environment:** Google Workspace (including Gmail, Google Drive, and Google Calendar). Greenfield Organics had utilized Google Workspace as its primary email and collaboration platform since approximately 2014, and accordingly the source environment contained historical email data spanning from the earliest available messages --- dating to approximately January 2014 --- through the migration cutover date in late August 2023. The full historical archive, including all messages from the January 2014 through August 2023 period, was within scope for migration.

**Target Environment:** Microsoft 365, including Outlook/Exchange Online for email, OneDrive for Business for individual file storage, and SharePoint Online for shared document libraries and collaboration.

**Scope of Data Migrated:** The engagement encompassed the migration of all historical email data, calendar entries, contacts, and Google Drive files for all active and inactive user accounts maintained in the Google Workspace environment. The migration covered all three of Greenfield Organics\' office locations:

> • Raleigh, North Carolina (corporate headquarters)
>
> • Bend, Oregon
>
> • Boise, Idaho

**Migration Methodology:** The migration was performed using Cloudbridge\'s proprietary migration toolset and was executed in phased batches organized by department and facility location. Each batch was validated against source-environment message counts prior to the commencement of the subsequent batch. The phased approach was designed to minimize disruption to end-user productivity during the transition period.

**[3. Migration Results and Statistics]{.underline}**

The following is a detailed summary of migration outcomes for email message data:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Metric**                                      **Count**               **Percentage**
  ----------------------------------------------- ----------------------- -----------------------
  Total email messages identified for migration   \~370,000               100%

  Successfully migrated                           \~355,200               96%

  Failed / not migrated                           \~14,800                4%
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The approximately 14,800 messages that were not successfully migrated fall into two principal failure categories:

**Message Formatting Incompatibilities --- approximately 9,100 messages (\~61% of total failures).** These failures involved messages with non-standard MIME encoding, legacy rich-text formatting, or messages that had been originally composed in third-party email clients that introduced formatting artifacts incompatible with the Exchange Online import process. In many cases, these messages contained malformed headers or non-compliant character encoding that caused the import routine to reject the message rather than risk data corruption in the target mailbox.

**Embedded Object Corruption --- approximately 5,700 messages (\~39% of total failures).** These failures involved messages containing embedded images, inline attachments, or OLE (Object Linking and Embedding) objects that were corrupted during the extraction process from Google Workspace and could not be reconstituted in the format required by Exchange Online. The corruption appears to have originated during the export phase, where certain binary-encoded embedded objects were rendered unreadable by the migration tooling.

Notably, the 14,800 failed messages are distributed across approximately 340 unique mailboxes, meaning the failures were not concentrated within a single user account or department but rather spread broadly across the organization. No single mailbox accounted for a disproportionately large share of the failed messages.

Cloudbridge attempted two additional re-processing passes on the full set of failed messages using alternative extraction parameters and encoding-correction routines. Neither pass resolved the underlying formatting and corruption issues, and the messages remained in a non-migratable state following these efforts.

Cloudbridge does not retain or hold copies of the failed messages. The original messages remained in the source Google Workspace environment following the completion of the migration and the re-processing attempts. Any recovery of these messages would depend on access to the source environment.

**[4. Source Environment Decommissioning]{.underline}**

Following completion of the migration and delivery of this report in draft form to the Client\'s IT department, Cloudbridge received instructions from Greenfield Organics\' IT department to assist with decommissioning the source Google Workspace environment. Per client instruction, the Google Workspace environment was decommissioned on October 1, 2023. In this context, \"decommissioned\" means that all Google Workspace user licenses were terminated, all user accounts were deleted from the Google Workspace administration console, and all associated data stores --- including Gmail mailbox data, Google Drive file storage, and Google Calendar data --- were removed.

Prior to decommissioning, Cloudbridge recommended to the Client that a backup or archival copy of the source Google Workspace environment be maintained, particularly with respect to any data that was not successfully migrated to the target environment. The decision to proceed with decommissioning was made by the Client. Cloudbridge was not informed whether any separate backup or archival copy of the approximately 14,800 unmigrated email messages was created by the Client or any third party prior to the decommissioning of the Google Workspace environment.

Cloudbridge notes that Google Workspace data deletion following license termination is subject to Google\'s standard data retention and purge policies. Recovery of data after decommissioning and account deletion may not be possible, and the feasibility of any recovery effort is outside of Cloudbridge\'s control and would be governed entirely by Google\'s policies and technical capabilities.

**[5. Recommendations]{.underline}**

Based on the results of this engagement, Cloudbridge offers the following recommendations to Greenfield Organics:

1\. **Data Integrity Verification.** Greenfield should conduct spot-check audits of migrated data within the Microsoft 365 environment to verify the integrity and completeness of email messages, calendar entries, contacts, and files across a representative sample of user mailboxes and departments.

2\. **Recovery of Unmigrated Messages.** If recovery of the approximately 14,800 unmigrated email messages is desired, Greenfield should contact Google\'s enterprise support team promptly to determine whether any data can be recovered from the decommissioned Google Workspace environment. The likelihood of successful data recovery decreases over time following account deletion and license termination, and Greenfield is encouraged to initiate any such inquiry without delay.

3\. **Retention of Migration Documentation.** Greenfield should maintain a copy of this report, together with any associated migration logs and correspondence, for compliance, audit, and recordkeeping purposes.

4\. **Further Assistance.** Cloudbridge remains available to assist with any further data recovery efforts should source data be obtained from Google or from any backup or archival copy that may exist. Please contact us at the information provided below to discuss any follow-up needs.

**[6. Report Certification and Contact Information]{.underline}**

This report was prepared and certified by the following Cloudbridge Solutions personnel:

**Prepared by:**

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

Marcus Hwang Senior Migration Engineer Cloudbridge Solutions

**Reviewed by:**

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

Rachel Donovan Director of Enterprise Services Cloudbridge Solutions

**Contact Information:** Cloudbridge Solutions 3400 Glenwood Avenue, Suite 210 Raleigh, NC 27612 Tel: (919) 555-0184

Email: enterprise@cloudbridgesolutions.com

**[COMMON INTEREST AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

**Dated as of September 15, 2021**

This Common Interest Agreement (this \"Agreement\") is entered into as of September 15, 2021, by and between **Thornwell & Pratt LLP**, 1200 K Street NW, Suite 800, Washington, DC 20005 (\"T&P\"), counsel for **Greenfield Organics, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 2100 Capital Boulevard, Raleigh, North Carolina 27604 (\"Greenfield\"), and **Fielding & Acosta LLP**, 600 Congress Avenue, Suite 2400, Austin, Texas 78701 (\"F&A\"), counsel for **NourishCo Holdings, LLC**, a Texas limited liability company with its principal place of business at 4500 Bee Caves Road, Suite 310, Austin, Texas 78746 (\"NourishCo\"). Greenfield and NourishCo are collectively referred to herein as the \"Common Interest Parties,\" and T&P and F&A are collectively referred to herein as \"Counsel.\"

Both Greenfield and NourishCo are defendants in the matter captioned *In re Organic Baby Food Labeling Litigation*, Case No. 3:21-cv-04187 (W.D. Tex.) (the \"Labeling Litigation\"), a putative class action alleging, among other things, that the Common Interest Parties engaged in deceptive labeling and marketing practices with respect to certain organic baby food products. The Common Interest Parties share a common legal interest in the defense of the Labeling Litigation and wish to facilitate the exchange of privileged and work-product-protected information between their respective Counsel in furtherance of that common legal interest in the defense of the Labeling Litigation, without waiving any applicable privilege, protection, or immunity from disclosure. This Agreement memorializes the terms and conditions upon which such exchange shall take place.

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS**, Greenfield and NourishCo are co-defendants in the Labeling Litigation, a putative class action concerning allegations related to the labeling and marketing of organic baby food products in alleged violation of various federal and state consumer protection statutes, including the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices---Consumer Protection Act;

**WHEREAS**, the Common Interest Parties share a common legal interest in defending against the claims asserted in the Labeling Litigation, including the development of common factual and legal positions in response to the allegations contained in the Consolidated Amended Class Action Complaint;

**WHEREAS**, in the course of the defense of the Labeling Litigation, Counsel for each Common Interest Party may find it necessary or desirable to share certain privileged communications, attorney work product, and other confidential information with the other party\'s Counsel to facilitate the coordinated and efficient defense of the Labeling Litigation;

**WHEREAS**, the Common Interest Parties intend that such sharing shall not constitute a waiver of any applicable privilege, including but not limited to the attorney-client privilege, the work product doctrine, the joint defense privilege, or any other applicable protection or immunity from disclosure under federal or state law; and

**WHEREAS**, the Common Interest Parties wish to memorialize the terms upon which such sharing shall occur, and to set forth their mutual understandings with respect to the treatment and protection of shared materials.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the foregoing premises and the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, the parties agree as follows:

**[Section 1. Definitions]{.underline}**

As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:

1.1 **\"Common Interest Materials\"** means all communications between Counsel for the Common Interest Parties relating to the defense of the Labeling Litigation, including but not limited to memoranda, analyses, legal research, factual summaries, document compilations, deposition preparation materials, litigation strategy discussions, draft pleadings and motions, expert reports and analyses, settlement analyses, damage calculations, and any other privileged or work-product-protected materials shared between Counsel pursuant to this Agreement. Common Interest Materials shall also include any notes, summaries, or derivative works created by one party\'s Counsel based upon or reflecting the substance of materials shared by the other party\'s Counsel in connection with the defense of the Labeling Litigation.

1.2 **\"Labeling Litigation\"** means *In re Organic Baby Food Labeling Litigation*, Case No. 3:21-cv-04187 (W.D. Tex.), including all claims and counterclaims asserted therein, all motions and proceedings related thereto, and any appeals therefrom.

1.3 **\"Common Interest Parties\"** means Greenfield Organics, Inc. and NourishCo Holdings, LLC.

1.4 **\"Counsel\"** means Thornwell & Pratt LLP and Fielding & Acosta LLP, and their respective partners, associates, attorneys, paralegals, legal assistants, and staff involved in the defense of the Labeling Litigation.

**[Section 2. Common Legal Interest]{.underline}**

2.1 The parties acknowledge and agree that the Common Interest Parties share a common legal interest in the defense of the Labeling Litigation. This common legal interest arises from the fact that both Greenfield and NourishCo are named as defendants in the Labeling Litigation and face substantially similar allegations concerning the labeling and marketing of organic baby food products.

2.2 The exchange of Common Interest Materials pursuant to this Agreement is undertaken solely in furtherance of this common legal interest in the defense of the Labeling Litigation. All communications between Counsel made pursuant to this Agreement are intended to be protected by the common interest doctrine, the attorney-client privilege, the work product doctrine, and any other applicable privilege or protection.

2.3 Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as creating a joint defense, agency, partnership, joint venture, or attorney-client relationship between a Common Interest Party and the Counsel of the other Common Interest Party. Each Common Interest Party shall remain separately represented by its own Counsel, and nothing herein shall require either party to take any action or adopt any litigation strategy proposed by the other. Each party\'s Counsel owes professional duties and obligations solely to its own client and not to the other Common Interest Party.

**[Section 3. Scope and Permitted Use of Common Interest Materials]{.underline}**

3.1 Common Interest Materials shall be used solely for the purpose of the defense of the Labeling Litigation. No Common Interest Party or its Counsel shall use Common Interest Materials received from the other party for any purpose other than the defense of the Labeling Litigation, including but not limited to any business purpose, competitive purpose, regulatory purpose, or any other litigation, proceeding, investigation, or dispute.

3.2 Common Interest Materials shall not be disclosed, disseminated, or made available to any third party without the prior written consent of all Counsel. For the avoidance of doubt, \"third party\" includes any other counsel, consultant, expert, or advisor not identified in this Agreement, unless such person has been retained specifically for the defense of the Labeling Litigation and has agreed in writing to be bound by the terms of this Agreement.

3.3 Each party\'s Counsel shall maintain Common Interest Materials in a manner consistent with the protection of applicable privileges, including storing such materials separately from non-privileged files where practicable and marking such materials as privileged and confidential.

3.4 Access to Common Interest Materials within each Common Interest Party\'s organization shall be limited to those individuals who have a need to know for purposes of the defense of the Labeling Litigation, including in-house counsel, and such employees or agents as Counsel may reasonably determine require access for purposes of the defense. Counsel shall use reasonable efforts to inform any such employees or agents of the confidential and privileged nature of the Common Interest Materials and the restrictions on their use and disclosure.

**[Section 4. Preservation of Privileges]{.underline}**

4.1 The sharing of Common Interest Materials pursuant to this Agreement shall not constitute a waiver of any applicable privilege, including without limitation the attorney-client privilege, the work product doctrine, the common interest privilege, or any other applicable protection or immunity from disclosure. The parties expressly intend that the exchange of Common Interest Materials under this Agreement is made in furtherance of a common legal interest and that such exchange shall be fully protected from disclosure to any third party.

4.2 Each Common Interest Party retains the right to assert all applicable privileges with respect to Common Interest Materials in any proceeding, whether currently pending or hereafter commenced.

4.3 No Common Interest Party or its Counsel may waive any privilege applicable to Common Interest Materials shared by the other Common Interest Party or its Counsel without the prior written consent of the disclosing party\'s Counsel. Any purported waiver made without such consent shall be deemed ineffective and without force or effect.

4.4 In the event that a third party, including any court, administrative body, governmental agency, or private litigant, seeks disclosure of Common Interest Materials, each party agrees to: (a) promptly notify the other party\'s Counsel of such request or demand, and in any event within five (5) business days of receiving notice thereof; (b) assert all applicable privileges and protections with respect to such Common Interest Materials; and (c) take reasonable steps to resist such disclosure pending resolution of the privilege claim, including by filing motions for protective orders or other appropriate relief.

**[Section 5. Withdrawal]{.underline}**

5.1 Either party may withdraw from this Agreement by providing written notice to the other party\'s Counsel. Such notice shall be delivered in accordance with the notice provisions set forth in Section 7.6 of this Agreement.

5.2 Upon withdrawal, the withdrawing party and its Counsel shall continue to be bound by the confidentiality obligations set forth in this Agreement with respect to all Common Interest Materials received prior to the effective date of withdrawal. The withdrawing party shall not disclose, use, or rely upon any Common Interest Materials received from the other party for any purpose whatsoever following withdrawal.

5.3 Withdrawal shall not affect any privilege that attached to Common Interest Materials prior to the date of withdrawal. The parties acknowledge that the privileged character of Common Interest Materials shared prior to withdrawal shall survive such withdrawal.

**[Section 6. No Obligation to Share]{.underline}**

6.1 Nothing in this Agreement shall obligate any Common Interest Party or its Counsel to share any information, documents, or materials with the other Common Interest Party or its Counsel. The decision to share or not to share particular materials shall be made at the sole and absolute discretion of each Common Interest Party and its Counsel.

6.2 Each Common Interest Party and its Counsel retains sole discretion over what, if any, Common Interest Materials to share with the other party\'s Counsel, and over the timing and manner of any such sharing.

6.3 The decision not to share particular materials shall not give rise to any inference, presumption, or adverse consequence of any kind, and shall not be deemed a breach of this Agreement or of any duty owed by one Common Interest Party to the other.

**[Section 7. Miscellaneous]{.underline}**

7.1 **Governing Law.** This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Texas, without regard to its conflict of laws principles. The parties consent to the exclusive jurisdiction of the federal and state courts located in the Western District of Texas for any disputes arising under or relating to this Agreement.

7.2 **Entire Agreement.** This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous discussions, negotiations, understandings, and agreements, whether written or oral, relating to the subject matter of this Agreement.

7.3 **Amendment.** This Agreement may be amended, modified, or supplemented only by a written instrument signed by all Counsel. No waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall be effective unless set forth in a written instrument signed by the party granting such waiver.

7.4 **Counterparts.** This Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Execution and delivery of this Agreement by facsimile or electronic transmission (including PDF) shall be deemed to be, and shall have the same legal effect as, execution and delivery of an original.

7.5 **No Third-Party Beneficiaries.** This Agreement is for the sole benefit of the parties hereto and their respective clients, and nothing contained herein, express or implied, is intended to or shall confer upon any other person or entity any legal or equitable right, benefit, or remedy of any nature whatsoever under or by reason of this Agreement.

7.6 **Notices.** All notices, requests, consents, and other communications under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed duly given when delivered personally, sent by overnight courier (with confirmation of delivery), or sent by electronic mail (with confirmation of receipt) to Counsel at the following addresses:

22	
23	**[Section 1: Purpose and Scope]{.underline}**
24	
25	The purpose of this Document Retention and Information Management Policy (this \"Policy\") is to establish uniform standards for the creation, retention, archival, and destruction of business records and electronic data across Greenfield Organics, Inc. (\"Greenfield\" or the \"Company\"), a Delaware corporation headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina. This Policy applies to all records in any format, including paper, electronic, digital, audio, and visual, and covers all departments and all facilities of the Company, including the Company\'s headquarters in Raleigh, North Carolina, and its operating facilities in Bend, Oregon and Boise, Idaho.
26	
27	This Policy applies to all of the Company\'s approximately 1,840 employees, as well as all contractors, consultants, and temporary personnel performing work on behalf of the Company. The goals of this Policy are to: (a) ensure the Company\'s compliance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements governing the retention of business records; (b) support efficient business operations by promoting an organized and consistent approach to records management; and (c) manage storage costs, both physical and electronic, by ensuring that records are retained only for the periods necessary to satisfy legal, regulatory, and business requirements.
28	
29	Records should be retained only for the periods specified herein and destroyed in the ordinary course of business upon expiration of the applicable retention period. Adherence to the retention periods and destruction schedules set forth in this Policy ensures that the Company maintains the records it needs while disposing of records that are no longer required in a timely, cost-effective manner.
30	
31	**[Section 2: Definitions]{.underline}**
32	
33	For purposes of this Policy, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:
34	
35	**\"Business Record\"** means any document, communication, file, or data created, received, or maintained by Company personnel in connection with Company business, regardless of format or medium.
36	
37	**\"Electronic Communication\"** means email, instant messages, text messages, chat messages (including those sent via Slack, Microsoft Teams, or any successor platform), voicemail, and any other electronically transmitted communication created, sent, or received using Company-provided systems or accounts.
38	
39	**\"Document\"** is broadly defined to include paper and electronic records, correspondence, memoranda, reports, analyses, presentations, spreadsheets, databases, calendars, notes, and any other recorded information, whether in hard copy or stored electronically.
40	
41	**\"Retention Period\"** means the minimum period during which a record falling within a particular category must be retained before it is eligible for destruction in accordance with this Policy.
42	
43	**\"Archival\"** means the process of moving records from active storage to long-term storage, during which the records remain accessible but are no longer in primary or everyday use.
44	
45	**\"Destruction\"** means the permanent deletion, shredding, or other irreversible disposal of records such that the records can no longer be retrieved, reconstructed, or accessed.
46	
47	**\"Responsible Department\"** means the department primarily responsible for maintaining records of a particular category, as designated in the retention schedule set forth in Section 4 of this Policy.
48	
49	**\"Record Custodian\"** means the individual designated within each Responsible Department to oversee day-to-day compliance with this Policy and to serve as the primary point of contact for records management matters within that department.
50	
51	**[Section 3: General Retention Principles]{.underline}**
52	
53	The following general principles govern the retention and destruction of records under this Policy:
54	
55	Records should be retained for the minimum period required by applicable law, regulation, or documented business need, as specified in the retention schedule set forth in Section 4 of this Policy. Upon expiration of the applicable Retention Period, records should be destroyed in the ordinary course of business. The Company\'s goal is to ensure that records are neither retained longer than necessary nor destroyed before the applicable Retention Period has expired.
56	
57	Destruction of records should occur on a regular, systematic basis. The Company recommends that each department conduct a quarterly review of its records to identify records that have reached the end of their applicable Retention Periods and are eligible for destruction. Systematic, periodic destruction helps the Company manage storage costs, reduce the volume of records maintained, and ensure consistency in records management practices across all departments and facilities.
58	
59	Employees should not retain duplicate copies of records beyond the applicable Retention Period. Where a record exists in multiple copies or in both paper and electronic formats, the Responsible Department should designate one authoritative copy as the official Company record, and all other copies should be destroyed upon expiration of the applicable Retention Period.
60	
61	All Retention Periods are measured from the date of creation or receipt of the record, unless otherwise specified in Section 4. Records related to ongoing projects, active customer engagements, or other matters that are not yet concluded should be retained until the project or matter is concluded, after which the applicable Retention Period begins to run from the date of conclusion.
62	
63	**[Section 4: Retention Schedule by Record Category]{.underline}**
64	
65	The following sections set forth the retention schedules applicable to the major categories of Company records. Where a specific record could fall into more than one category, the longer Retention Period shall apply.
66	
67	**Section 4.1: Email Communications**
68	
69	Email communications are an essential tool for Company business and are subject to the following retention schedule:
70	
71	**Platform:** Email communications are maintained on the Company\'s enterprise email platform. All employees are expected to use the Company-provided email system as their primary means of business email communication.
72	
73	**Active Retention:** Email messages shall remain in the sender\'s or recipient\'s active mailbox for a period of two (2) years from the date of creation or receipt. During the active retention period, email messages are fully accessible to the user and may be searched, forwarded, and otherwise used in the normal course of business.
74	
75	**Archival:** After the two-year active retention period, email messages shall be automatically moved to the Company\'s archival storage system, where they shall be maintained in a searchable, read-only format. Archived emails may be accessed by the user or by the IT Department upon request, but they are no longer maintained in the user\'s active mailbox. Email auto-archival after two (2) years occurs through automated system processes administered by the IT Department.
76	
77	**Destruction:** Archived email messages shall be permanently deleted five (5) years from the date of creation or receipt through automated system processes. Following the five-year total retention window, emails are permanently purged from the archival system and are no longer recoverable. Email auto-archival after 2 years with deletion after 5 years is the Company\'s standard email lifecycle.
78	
79	Employees are discouraged from maintaining personal archives of email messages outside the Company\'s email system. Attachments to email messages follow the retention schedule of the email itself, unless the attachment independently falls within a record category that has a longer Retention Period under this Policy. For example, a contract attached to an email would follow the contract retention schedule set forth in Section 4.5, and should be separately saved to the appropriate file share or document management system.
80	
81	**Section 4.2: Instant Messaging and Chat Platforms (Slack / Messaging Applications)**
82	
83	Instant messaging and chat platforms are used at the Company for informal, real-time collaboration. As of the date of this Policy, the Company uses Slack as its primary instant messaging and chat platform. The Company may migrate to alternative platforms in the future; if so, the same retention schedule shall apply to the successor platform unless this Policy is amended.
84	
85	**Retention Period:** All messages transmitted via Slack or any successor instant messaging or chat platform shall be automatically deleted ninety (90) days after creation. This 90-day auto-deletion applies to all Slack content, including channels (public and private), direct messages, and group messages.
86	
87	**Rationale:** Instant messages are intended for informal, transient communications and are not intended to serve as the Company\'s official business records. Employees should not use instant messaging platforms for communications that constitute formal business decisions or that are required to be retained under any other provision of this Policy. Where an instant message discussion results in a decision, action item, or other substantive business outcome, the responsible employee should memorialize that outcome in a more permanent format, such as an email or a document saved to the appropriate file share.
88	
89	**No Archival Step:** Unlike email, instant messages are not moved to an archival system prior to deletion. Messages proceed directly from active status to permanent deletion after the 90-day retention window.
90	
91	**Files Shared via Slack:** Files uploaded to or shared through Slack are also subject to the 90-day deletion schedule, unless the employee separately saves the file to a shared network drive, document management system, or other Company-approved storage location. Employees are responsible for ensuring that any files shared via Slack that have independent retention value are saved outside of the Slack environment before the 90-day deletion window expires.
92	
93	**Section 4.3: File Shares and Document Management Systems**
94	
95	Business documents stored on shared network drives, SharePoint sites, and any cloud-based document storage systems approved by the Company shall be retained for the Retention Period applicable to the relevant record category as set forth elsewhere in this Section 4. Departments are responsible for organizing their file shares in a logical manner and for periodically reviewing stored documents to identify records that are eligible for destruction.
96	
97	The Company recommends that departments conduct an annual review of file share contents to ensure compliance with this Policy and to remove records that have exceeded their applicable Retention Periods. Draft documents and working copies should be deleted once a final version has been stored in the appropriate location, unless the drafts reflect substantive changes that are relevant to compliance or regulatory obligations. Responsible Departments should establish folder structures and naming conventions that facilitate organized retention and timely identification of records eligible for destruction.

Employees shall not use personal devices, personal email accounts, personal cloud storage services, or other unauthorized systems to preserve copies of Company records that are subject to automated deletion. Any employee who becomes aware that automated deletion processes are not functioning as intended should promptly notify the IT Department.

231	**[Section 6: Roles and Responsibilities]{.underline}**
232	
233	The following roles and responsibilities are established for the administration and enforcement of this Policy:

235	**General Counsel (David Yun-Nakamura):** The General Counsel oversees overall compliance with this Policy and provides guidance to departments and employees on legal requirements affecting record retention. The General Counsel serves as the final authority on questions of record classification and the appropriate Retention Period for records not expressly addressed in Section 4 of this Policy. The General Counsel is responsible for ensuring that the Policy is reviewed and updated on a regular basis in accordance with Section 8.
236	
237	**Department Heads:** Each Department Head is responsible for ensuring that personnel within his or her department comply with this Policy. Department Heads shall designate one or more Record Custodians within their departments and shall conduct an annual review of departmental records to confirm that retention and destruction activities are being carried out in accordance with the schedules set forth in this Policy.
238	
239	**Record Custodians:** Record Custodians are the individuals designated by Department Heads within each Responsible Department to oversee day-to-day compliance with this Policy. Record Custodians are responsible for maintaining departmental retention inventories, coordinating with the IT Department regarding scheduled destruction of electronic records, and serving as the primary point of contact for records management inquiries within their departments.
240	
241	**IT Department:** The IT Department is responsible for implementing and maintaining the automated retention and deletion systems described in Section 5 of this Policy. IT ensures the proper functioning of archival and destruction processes across all Company electronic data systems and maintains destruction logs as required by this Policy.
242	
243	**All Employees:** All employees are expected to comply with this Policy. Employees shall not destroy records outside the normal automated or scheduled destruction processes, and employees shall not retain records beyond the applicable Retention Period except as specifically instructed by the Legal Department. Employees with questions regarding their obligations under this Policy should contact their departmental Record Custodian or the Legal Department.
244	
245	**[Section 7: Compliance and Enforcement]{.underline}**
246	
247	All employees, contractors, and temporary workers of the Company are required to comply with this Policy. Failure to comply with any provision of this Policy may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment or engagement.
248	
249	Specific violations of this Policy include, without limitation:
250	
251	> \(a\) Destroying records before the expiration of the applicable Retention Period, other than through the normal automated deletion processes described in this Policy;
252	>
253	> \(b\) Retaining records beyond the applicable Retention Period without prior authorization from the Legal Department;
254	>
255	> \(c\) Storing Company records on personal devices, personal email accounts, or unauthorized cloud storage services without prior written approval from the employee\'s Department Head and the IT Department; and
256	>
257	> \(d\) Interfering with or circumventing automated retention, archival, or deletion processes implemented by the IT Department.
258	
259	Employees should not use personal devices or personal accounts to create, transmit, or store Company business records. Where an employee has inadvertently stored Company records on a personal device or account, the employee should promptly transfer those records to the appropriate Company system and delete the personal copies.
260	
261	The Legal Department will conduct periodic audits of compliance with this Policy. Such audits may include review of email and messaging systems, file shares, and departmental retention inventories. Questions about this Policy, including questions about the classification of a particular record or the applicable Retention Period, should be directed to the Legal Department.

265	This Policy may be amended from time to time by the General Counsel with the approval of the Chief Executive Officer. Amendments to this Policy shall be communicated to all employees via company-wide email and shall be posted on the Company\'s intranet. Employees are responsible for reviewing and familiarizing themselves with any amendments to this Policy promptly upon receipt of notice.

Department Heads and Record Custodians may suggest revisions to the Legal Department at any time.

**ORGANIC INFANT NUTRITION TRADE ASSOCIATION** 1750 Rhode Island Avenue NW, Suite 400 Washington, DC 20036

Pamela Sievert, Executive Director

**[OINTA Pricing Index Database --- Member Information Guide]{.underline}**

**Revised January 2023**

**[About OINTA]{.underline}**

The Organic Infant Nutrition Trade Association (\"OINTA\") is a nonprofit trade association founded in 2012 and headquartered in Washington, D.C. OINTA\'s mission is to promote the organic infant and toddler nutrition industry, advocate for sound regulatory policy at the federal and state levels, and provide members with valuable market intelligence and networking opportunities. Since its founding, OINTA has grown to become the leading voice for organic baby food manufacturers and distributors in the United States.

OINTA hosts biannual Market Strategy Summits each April and October. These summits serve as the premier industry forums for discussion of market trends, regulatory developments, and best practices among organic infant nutrition companies. The summits bring together senior executives, marketing leaders, and operations professionals from across the membership for two days of presentations, panel discussions, and networking. OINTA is led by Executive Director Pamela Sievert, who has guided the organization\'s strategic direction since 2016.

**[OINTA Membership]{.underline}**

OINTA currently comprises seven member companies representing a broad cross-section of the organic infant and toddler nutrition market. Membership is open to any U.S.-based manufacturer or distributor of organic infant or toddler nutrition products. Our current members are:

1\. **Greenfield Organics, Inc.** --- Raleigh, NC

2\. **NourishCo Holdings, LLC** --- Austin, TX

3\. **Verdant Baby Foods, Inc.** --- Portland, OR

4\. **Little Acres Nutrition Co.** --- Minneapolis, MN

5\. **Sproutwell Organics, LLC** --- Boulder, CO

6\. **Canopy Infant Products, Inc.** --- Savannah, GA

7\. **Bright Meadow Foods, LLC** --- Sacramento, CA

All members participate in OINTA programs, including the biannual Market Strategy Summits, regulatory advocacy initiatives on Capitol Hill and before the FDA, and the Pricing Index Database described in this guide. Annual membership dues are scaled based on company revenue to ensure that organizations of all sizes can participate fully in the association\'s programs and benefit from its resources. For information regarding current dues schedules, please contact the OINTA office directly.

**[Pricing Index Database --- Overview]{.underline}**

The Pricing Index Database is OINTA\'s flagship market intelligence tool. Launched in 2017 in response to member demand for better visibility into industry-wide pricing dynamics, the database has quickly become one of the most valued benefits of OINTA membership.

The purpose of the Pricing Index Database is to provide members with aggregated benchmarking data on wholesale pricing trends in the organic infant and toddler nutrition market. The database is designed to promote transparency and informed decision-making among members, enabling companies to understand where their pricing stands relative to industry averages and to identify emerging trends across reporting periods.

Participation in the Pricing Index Database is included as a core benefit of OINTA membership, and all members are encouraged to contribute their data each quarter. The database is accessible exclusively to OINTA member companies through a password-protected section of the OINTA member portal. Non-members do not have access to the database or its published reports.

**[Data Reporting Requirements]{.underline}**

Each participating member company reports its **average wholesale price per ounce** across its organic baby food product lines on a quarterly basis. Data is reported at the company level --- that is, each member submits a single averaged figure representing its entire organic infant and toddler product portfolio, rather than disaggregated data by individual product, SKU, or brand.

**Reporting frequency and deadlines.** Data is reported on a quarterly basis aligned with the calendar year. Reporting deadlines fall thirty (30) days after the close of each calendar quarter, as follows:

> • **Q1 (January -- March):** Report due by April 30
>
> • **Q2 (April -- June):** Report due by July 31
>
> • **Q3 (July -- September):** Report due by October 31
>
> • **Q4 (October -- December):** Report due by January 31

**Reporting format.** Members submit data through a standardized online reporting form available on the OINTA member portal. Each quarterly submission includes the following data points: (a) the member company name, (b) the applicable reporting quarter, (c) the average wholesale price per ounce (in U.S. dollars) for organic baby food products sold during the quarter, and (d) the total volume shipped (in ounces) for the quarter.

**Participation.** Reporting is voluntary but strongly encouraged. We are pleased to note that, historically, all member companies have participated in each quarterly reporting cycle since the database\'s inception in 2017. This high rate of participation ensures the reliability and comprehensiveness of the published index.

It is important to emphasize that reported prices reflect **actual average wholesale prices** --- that is, real transaction-level pricing based on invoiced sales --- rather than list prices, manufacturer\'s suggested retail prices (MSRPs), or other non-transactional figures. This ensures that the index accurately captures genuine market conditions.

**[Data Publication and the One-Quarter Lag]{.underline}**

OINTA publishes the Pricing Index Database results to all members on a quarterly basis. To allow adequate time for data collection, verification, and compilation, published data reflects pricing from **one quarter prior** to the publication date. In other words, there is a one-quarter lag between the reporting period and the date on which results are made available to members. For example, data reported for Q1 (January through March) is compiled and published to members during Q2, typically by mid-May.

**Published data points.** Each quarterly Pricing Index Database report includes the following:

> • The **simple average** of all member-reported average wholesale prices per ounce for the applicable quarter;
>
> • The **high value** and **low value** among member-reported average wholesale prices for the quarter (reported without identifying the submitting companies); and
>
> • The **total industry volume**, calculated as the sum of all member-reported shipment volumes (in ounces) for the quarter.

OINTA does not publish individual company data. All published figures represent aggregated or averaged data points. The published index is distributed as a PDF report through the member portal and is also presented and discussed at the next scheduled Market Strategy Summit, giving members the opportunity to review the results in a collaborative setting alongside their industry peers.

**[Data Confidentiality and Use Restrictions]{.underline}**

OINTA treats all member-submitted data as confidential. Individual company submissions are accessible only to OINTA staff members responsible for compiling the quarterly index and are not shared with other members or any third parties in disaggregated form.

Members may use published Pricing Index Database reports solely for internal benchmarking and strategic planning purposes. Members may not redistribute published data, in whole or in part, to non-members, media outlets, or any other external parties without prior written consent from OINTA.

OINTA does not provide legal advice regarding members\' use of Pricing Index Database information. Members are responsible for ensuring their own compliance with all applicable laws and regulations in connection with their use of OINTA programs and published data. Questions regarding the interpretation or application of published data should be directed to members\' own professional advisors.

**[Contact Information]{.underline}**

For questions about the Pricing Index Database, OINTA membership, or any of our programs, please contact:

> **Pamela Sievert, Executive Director** Organic Infant Nutrition Trade Association 1750 Rhode Island Avenue NW, Suite 400 Washington, DC 20036
>
> Phone: (202) 555-0147
>
> Email: psievert@ointa.org
>
> Member Portal: www.ointa.org/members

© 2023 Organic Infant Nutrition Trade Association. All rights reserved. This document is provided for the exclusive use of OINTA members and prospective members.
